Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Paul Simon (politician)|Paul Simon]] chose to retire, rather than seek a third term in office. In the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary, [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Dick Durbin]] emerged victorious, while [[Illinois House of Representatives|state representative]] [[Al Salvi]] won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary. Though the election was initially anticipated to be close, Durbin ended up defeating Salvi by a comfortable double-digit margin of victory, allowing him to win what would be the first of five terms in the Senate. ==Background== The primaries and general elections coincided with those for other federal offices ([[1996 United States presidential election#Illinois|president]] and [[1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois|House]]), as well as those for [[1996 Illinois elections#State elections|state offices]]. For the primaries, turnout was 25.85%, with 1,583,406 votes cast.{{cite web |title=State of Illinois official vote cast at the primary election held on ... |url=https://archive.org/details/stateofillinoiso1996illi/mode/2up |publisher=Illinois State Board of Elections |access-date=6 April 2020}} For the general election, turnout was 63.79%, with 4,250,722 votes cast.{{cite web |title=State of Illinois official vote cast at the general election .. |url=https://archive.org/details/stateofillinois1996illi/page/n7/mode/2up |publisher= Illinois State Board of Elections |access-date=6 April 2020}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * Jalil Ahmad, real estate agent * [[Dick Durbin]], incumbent [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] from [[Illinois's 20th congressional district]] * Ronald F.
